newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slip in lacklustre trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures lost ground in technically driven trade on Tuesday as a lack of fresh buying incentives prompted players to test the downside, dealers said.

They said the market showed little reaction to the release of Japan's revised May industrial output data, which showed a 4.5 percent increase from the previous month, compared with a preliminary estimate of a 3.8 percent rise.

"The figure was just a revision so there was not much of a reaction. Generally the market has factored in a good economy because the BOJ (Bank of Japan) keeps emphasising that the economy is recovering," a trader at a U.S. futures house said.
He said the Euroyen market looked slightly toppish on the charts and locals were keen to sell into any rallies.
The lead March Euroyen contract was quoted at 98.96 at 1122 GMT against an IMM close at 98.99.
Dealers said the contract looked well supported around its day low of 98.95.
"If 98.95 holds, we could see another rally to 99.06-99.10 before it comes back off," the trader said.
He said September JGBs looked relatively soft but should find support around 124.50 and the psychological 124.00 level.
The contract ended at 124.58 against its previous 124.88.
Eurodollar futures slipped ahead of the U.S. June retail sales report, due at 1230 GMT, and the June Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Wednesday.
"We should see a breakout of the recent ranges with the retail sales today and CPI tomorrow. I would buy on dips because the data out of the U.S. has been quite tame recently," the trader said.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.025 against an IMM close at 94.040. The contract is seen targetting the 94.190 level.
